structured_output.summary: The regression-and-governance chunk (attempt 2) delivers executed, independently-derived evidence and resolves every finding the maintainer dispositioned from attempt 1. Verified by reading the artifacts rather than the prose: (a) `tools/g25_fixtures.py:152` now uses `shutil.which('rustfmt')` with the home path only as fallback, matching the `generate_models.py` precedent; (b) null union branches are no longer silently skipped — `g25_fixtures.py:40,67` emits a `skippedBranches` inventory and `tools/test_g25_generation.py:70-76` asserts every skipped branch has a matching `type:null` case at the same root/path/choices; (c) the Python dict repr is gone from the published report — `tools/g25_report.py:165-167` renders mutation and format counts as Markdown code spans and `docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:45,47` shows the regenerated output; (d) the previously untested chunk CLI is now covered by six new tests (`tools/test_review_phase.py:407-498`) exercising real `main()` orchestration in a temporary git repo: chunk/rubric/decision record fields, `verify_record` with the right chunk vs. `None` vs. a wrong name, tampered chunk/rubric/decision fields, `--advance` rejection, missing `--scope-evidence`, historical-rubric rejection, and scope paths that are relative-escaping, absolute-external, symlinked outside the repo, or missing. The corpus remains traversal-derived and non-vacuous: 46 strict vendor response roots, 15,658 one-site mutations (now including six root-level type mutations per root), 184 format nodes, 138 enums, 55 typed projection fields; `tools/g25-oracle.mts` computes expectations independently from pinned vendor AJV and the actual frozen Zod modules after clearing the environment and making `fetch` throw (`:76-77`), requires a strict-valid witness per case (`:108`), and fails closed if a format/enum mutation is rejected (`:112`) or if the floor ever narrows TypeScript (`:113`). `crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs` executes all cases in Request plus both response modes with exact wire preservation and typed roundtrips, proves all eight format kinds tolerant across the whole SDK graph while keeping string typing strict and >100 Request-mode rejections, and `red_team_contracts.rs:2479-2515` drives the two typed public clients through caller transport with job-1/p-1/map-1, both reported timestamp forms, unknown enums and a u128-range number. Evidence is genuine: `docs/checks/phase-19.json` records all 23 commands of `check_phase.commands_for(19)` in exact order, all exit 0, `source_unchanged` true at the reviewed SHA 7edc9306…, the chunk snapshot is byte-consistent with it, the independent `phase-19-python-preflight.json` shows 294 Python tests OK at the same source hash, and the four new Rust test names appear as "… ok" in the 1.89.0 red-team, 1.99.0 red-team and 1.99.0 json-unification reports — so the newly-widened json-unification combination really executed the projection-number regression. The ledger now binds `auditSha256`, `casesSha256` and `outcomesSha256` (comparison.json:3,55964-55965), which with the two `--check` commands in one gate transitively pins corpus/oracle alignment. Remaining deficiencies are governance and traceability, not correctness: `review_phase.py` can still complete a phase without any accepted chunk review, the `casesSha256` guard it added to `g25_report.py` can never fire, a rejected chunk invocation leaves a stray snapshot, one test name overstates its scope, the `json-unification` feature-set remap silently drops the historical bare-core+arbitrary_precision combination, and the three disputed strict cases are covered only as unnamed generated rows. No blocker or high findings.

findings.description: Phase advancement still consults only the phase-level review record plus docs/checks; it never reads the per-phase "chunks" entries in docs/phase-status.json (lines 3776-3831) nor requires an accepted docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-*.json per chunk, and it never writes the accepted chunk totals back. This repeats attempt-01 finding 5 and is not mentioned in the recorded disposition (docs/phase-status.json:3838-3839), even though the plan's maintainer update (docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:132-136) states each chunk receives its own actual review with all five scores. With two of three phase-19 chunks currently recorded as unaccepted (typed-preservation total 39), the automated path would still allow `--phase 19 --verify ... --advance` to mark the phase complete. The chunk rule is enforced only by human discipline, inside the chunk whose scope is governance.
findings.required_fix: In main(), when uses_rubric(phase) and phases[phase] declares "chunks", require each chunk to have a verifiable record (verify_record(root, path, phase, before, chunk) True with decision in {accepted, accepted_with_deficiencies}) before setting status complete, record each accepted chunk total/categories in its chunk entry, and add a test in tools/test_review_phase.py that a phase with an unaccepted or missing chunk review cannot advance.

findings.description: The guard `if oracle.get('casesSha256') not in (None, hashlib.sha256(CASES.read_bytes()).hexdigest())` can never fire: tools/g25-oracle.mts:116 writes only {schemaVersion, roots, outcomes}, so the lookup is always None and the condition is always False. Attempt-01 finding 6 asked for a corpus digest inside outcomes.json asserted by the Rust test; the digests were instead placed in comparison.json (:55964-55965), which is a valid alternative binding, but the code added here reads like a safeguard while being dead.
findings.required_fix: Either emit casesSha256 in the outcomes.json envelope (tools/g25-oracle.mts:116) and require it unconditionally here and in crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs before zipping the arrays, or delete the vacuous conditional and state in a comment that cases/outcomes alignment is enforced by the paired --check gate commands and the ledger digests.

findings.description: The per-attempt checks snapshot is written (lines 311-315) before --scope-evidence paths are validated (lines 316-319), so a rejected chunk invocation leaves an orphan docs/reviews/phase-NN-chunk-X-attempt-01.checks.json behind. The existing attempt-collision guard at line 307 only inspects the .json record and .prompt.md, so the orphan is neither detected nor cleaned up; tools/test_review_phase.py:497-498 asserts only that no .prompt.md or .cli.json is left.
findings.required_fix: Move the scope-evidence resolution loop above the snapshot write (and above the destination-collision check if practical), and extend test_chunk_scope_must_resolve_to_existing_repository_path to assert no *.checks.json is created by a rejected invocation.

findings.description: test_vendor_bounds_are_request_only_and_frozen_bounds_are_untouched iterates self.graph, which is the vendor-compiled graph returned by red_team_dataplane.contract() (tools/red_team_dataplane.py:341), not the frozen SDK graph. It therefore proves only that vendor string min/max checks carry requestOnly; it never inspects a frozen bound, despite the name and despite docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:14 claiming existing TypeScript response bounds remain enforced. That claim actually rests on red_team_dataplane.py:241 setting requestOnly only in the vendor compiler plus test_red_team_dataplane.py:49-58 proving no frozen node changes.
findings.required_fix: Rename the test to reflect its vendor scope and add an explicit assertion that at least one frozen (non-vendor) ZodString min/max check in crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json lacks requestOnly, or add a Rust assertion that such a node still rejects an out-of-bounds string in both response modes.

findings.description: The shared FEATURES mapping now defines json-unification as ["--no-default-features", "--features", "red-team,serde_json/arbitrary_precision"]. The maintainer authorized adding Red Team (docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:138-141), but the previously accepted meaning was bare core + arbitrary_precision (see the recorded historical command in docs/checks/phase-03-rust-1.99.0-json-unification.json:36-48), and no feature set now runs that combination (minimal has no arbitrary_precision). Because commands_for() stores only the feature-set name, test_review_phase.ReviewGateTests.test_historical_phase_command_contracts_are_unchanged and the g10 maintenance-command test compare argument lists and cannot detect this remap.
findings.required_fix: Keep json-unification as the historical core+arbitrary_precision set and add a distinct name (for example red-team-json-unification) to the phase-19 gate and the CI matrix in .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90, or explicitly record in docs/PHASES.md/the plan that the bare-core+arbitrary_precision combination is intentionally retired and add a guard pinning each feature-set name to its resolved flag list.
